sources: Coursedog course search (POST /cm/ucberkeley_peoplesoft/courses/search/$filters, catalog hMSTjlpIK6VX5nnJn7ZE): CHINESE courses numbered 100-199 (91 courses); checked subject codes (JAPAN exists, JAPANESE doesn't)

why.reasoning: The catalog left this as a free-text placeholder saying 'at least 2'. The department requires three core courses, and the same section says: 'You may use CHINESE 7A (Introduction to Pre-modern Chinese Literature and Culture) or CHINESE 7B (Introduction to Modern Chinese Literature and Culture) to satisfy one of these three course requirements'. CHINESE 7A and 7B are therefore one shared group, so at most one of them counts. Each other group is one CHINESE course numbered 100-199 in the 2026-27 catalog (same upper-division test the generator's matching rules use). The department says 'upper-division', so this follows it rather than the catalog's ranges (100-194 plus graduate 200-296).

why.quote: Take two upper-division elective courses offered by the Department of East Asian Languages & Cultures (EALC).
why.reasoning: The catalog left this as a free-text placeholder. The department page goes on: 'Eligible electives include any upper-division courses with the following prefixes:' CHINESE, EALANG, JAPAN, KOREAN, MONGOLN, TIBETAN, which is what this matching rule checks (the catalog's 'JAPANESE' is the JAPAN subject code). Courses the core already counted are skipped. The catalog also allows CHINESE 7A/7B as an elective, but the department page says electives must be upper-division and mentions 7A/7B only for the core, so they're left out here. Graduate 200-level courses (which the catalog allows) aren't counted, because the department says 'upper-division'.

notStated: Whether graduate-level (200-296) EALC courses count as upper-division core or elective courses. The catalog allows them; the department page only says 'upper-division'.

Whether 195-199 courses (honors thesis H195A/B, group study 198, independent study 199) count. The catalog's ranges (100-194) leave them out; the department's 'any upper-division courses' seems to include them.
Whether CHINESE 7A/7B may count as an elective when not used for the core. The catalog says yes; the department page doesn't mention it.
notEncoded: Letter grades, 2.0 minimum GPA; P/NP only for CHINESE 10B/10X
One outside or study-abroad course by petition
